software_context.note: data-service runs a single uvicorn worker, so exactly one watcher daemon thread polls; the rate-limit window is that one process's memory (D-15).

sc1_loop_closure.interpretation: Latency is bounded below by the debounce window plus the capture-to-next-tick phase offset (up to one poll interval), plus the dg-reasoner SHACL round-trip.

sc2_runs_per_minute.capture_schedule: 4 captures at 1.0s intervals, then 8.0s idle, repeated for 60.0s
sc2_runs_per_minute.counting_rule: rows with status='completed' and trigger='auto' whose row completedAt falls in [window_start, window_end) -- read off the row, not off a stopwatch (P-13)

configuration.driver: poll_once driven directly against the live session with an injected unavailable shacl_fn; the daemon is parked on a 3600s debounce so it cannot race the ladder

list_runs_tolerance.consequence: list_validation_runs has no status filter, so captured, superseded and failed auto rows are returned to every existing reader alongside completed ones (D-12 accepted debt).

cypher_shapes.assumed_flag: 39-RESEARCH.md A2 discharged: all eight constants executed against live Neo4j without a Cypher error and produced the expected row shapes.

speckle_publish.ordering: P-07 inverted relative to the manual path: the run reached 'completed' with its verdict durable BEFORE the publish leg ran, and its status was observed to stay 'completed' throughout.
speckle_publish.speckle_config_source: the dev stack's existing Speckle configuration, discovered from DG project 'nonexistent-project-xyz' and re-pointed at 'p39-autoval'; p39-autoval is a synthetic phase-reserved project string with no Speckle project of its own
speckle_publish.note: The published version carries an empty entity and rules payload by construction: a captured DesignState envelope has no per-entity geometry and no failedRuleIds, so the version is a state-level marker rather than a coloured overlay. That emptiness is itself the Speckle-noise characteristic being measured — with the flag on, the observed auto-run Speckle-noise rate is 1 Speckle version per capture that survives debounce and the rate limiter, each version a near-empty commit appended to the project's dg-validation model.

row_lifecycle.how: The Wave 3 driver is `integration`-marked but NOT `live`-marked, so a bare in-container `pytest tests/ -q` collects it, and its module fixture deletes every :ValidationRun and :IntegrationConfig scoped to p39-autoval. That bare suite run was executed ~4 minutes after the publish leg as an acceptance check (the criterion 'the live module must NOT collect the publish leg'), and it destroyed the published run row as a side effect.
row_lifecycle.consequence: The Neo4j-side proof of this publish is no longer queryable; the Speckle-side proof is durable and independent. Speckle version 2ab708e884 in project 44088eefc6 / model a6d1e0c5da carries message 'DG validation run 0afe92c2e2324a85a988d42c4ffedc95' and created_at 2026-07-27T20:04:58.470Z, 0.97 s after the row's completedAt of 20:04:57.503Z. The run row was NOT recreated by hand and the publish leg was NOT re-run: D-11 permits exactly one publish-enabled run in the phase, and re-running would mint a second Speckle version, so the deletion is reported rather than repaired.

findings.title: An auto-run is SHACL-validated before its own ValidStatus exists, so every auto-run currently self-violates
findings.explanation: poll_once calls the sidecar and only then writes ValidStatus via COMPLETE_QUERY. At validation time the run node therefore has no ValidStatus, which trips the shapes graph's own Run shape. That finding's focusLabel is the runId, which matches no objState, so P-02's conservative unmapped fallback flips every ObjState entry to false.
findings.consequence: Auto-runs report a uniformly all-false ValidStatus regardless of the design's actual conformance. The verdict is structurally sound (it never claims a passing state it cannot attribute) but it is not yet discriminating. Ordering the ValidGraph export or scoping the shapes graph is an open design question for the DSAV-03 ADR, not something this investigation resolves.

findings.title: The rate limiter, not the debounce window, is what caps throughput under a sustained burst
findings.explanation: Captures that arrive while the limiter is saturated are skipped before coalesce, so their rows stay 'captured' rather than being superseded or dropped. They are picked up once the window drains.
findings.consequence: Throughput is capped without data loss, but a saturated project accumulates captured rows that existing readers already see (see list_runs_tolerance). The window is in-process and resets on restart (D-15).
